refuted.claim: core-sequence Item 1 (376abd3d4) — 'frame verdicts reach run stats': FrameAccepted/FrameRejected park (accepted, capture) in _gradedFrames and ExposureCompleted consumes it, so framesRejected and FilterStats.rejected are no longer structurally 0.
refuted.how: REFUTED as incomplete — the verdict reaches the COUNTERS but not the integration total printed beside them. /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq2/packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence_stats_provider.dart:140 recordFrame does `framesCaptured++; if (!accepted) framesRejected++; integrationSecs += exposureSecs;` — integrationSecs (and FilterStats.integrationSecs) is credited unconditionally, while the native side explicitly does NOT count rejected exposure time (see the FrameRejected doc at native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/node/progress.rs:210, 'integration budget tracker listens for this and skips counting the exposure time'). Counter-test run at HEAD against the batch's own harness (3x300s frames, frame 1 accepted, frames 2-3 rejected): `captured=3 rejected=2 integration=900.0`, breakdown `{M31: {Unknown: cap=3 rej=2 int=900.0}}`. Before the fix the record was consistently wrong (0 rejected / 900 s); after it the SAME record now contradicts itself — the Session Report, cockpit vitals and morning recap say '2 of 3 rejected' and '900 s integrated' on a night with 300 s of usable data. This is the moved-threshold shape: the verdict was routed to one consumer and not to the one that shares the sentence. Cross-check-frames-against-integration (N frames cannot total M seconds) now fails on any graded night.

refuted.claim: bridge-dart Item 6 (38dd72c41) — 'the inverted guard is dropped. There is no apiPhd2AutoSelectStar in the generated API, so the Dart client is the only implementation in either mode.'
refuted.how: REFUTED — relocated refusal. The guard removal is real (packages/skotiq_bridge/lib/src/bridge_stub/guiding_operations.dart:523-528 now goes straight to _phd2Client!.autoSelectStar()), but 'in either mode' is false. phd2Connect's native branch at the same file lines 25-30 reads `if (_nativeAvailable) { _phd2Client?.dispose(); _phd2Client = null; await gen_api.apiPhd2Connect(...); return; }` — line 125 is the ONLY assignment of _phd2Client and it sits after that early return, and phd2Disconnect (line 145) nulls it again. So on every build where the native library loads — the shipped desktop/headless configuration — _phd2Client is unconditionally null and phd2AutoSelectStar throws `Exception('PHD2 not connected')` on a rig whose PHD2 IS connected, via the Rust client. Auto-select is still unreachable in the mode users run; the baseline's nonsense refusal ('requires the native bridge') was replaced by a refusal that asserts something untrue about connection state — exactly the cry-wolf class. The batch's own note ('the refusal must name PHD2 connectivity, not a missing bridge') pins the new false message as the intended contract. Not reproducible under flutter test because _nativeAvailable is false there — which is why the batch's behavioural test passes on both the baseline and the fix; the source path is unambiguous.

refuted.claim: SEQ-12 (P0): "_handleNoEligibleTarget now only stops a run the autopilot itself dispatched" — the autopilot's ownership of the executor is truthful (reports/release-pass/impl/bfix-sequencing-autopilot.md:12).
refuted.how: Ran a throwaway engine test at HEAD (00ce2bf02) against the real SchedulerEngine with a gated sink: /tmp/claude-1000/.../scratchpad/seq12_race_test.dart, `flutter test` from packages/skotiq_core. Adjacent input = the tick racing a run START rather than mid-run. Sequence: autopilot dispatch in flight (sink blocks inside dispatchSequence) -> operator presses Stop autopilot -> SchedulerEngine.stop() runs to completion. Recorded call order: [dispatch-begin, stop, release, dispatch-end]. The stopSequence lands BEFORE the executor start returns, so the run the autopilot started begins AFTER the stop and nothing ever stops it — an orphan run exposing with the autopilot disengaged. Final engine status printed `SchedulerState.idle currentTargetId=1 name=Bode`: the idle autopilot also claims it owns a target, because the post-await `_updateStatus(currentTargetId: winner)` in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/scheduler/scheduler_engine/evaluation.dart:126-132 re-checks nothing after `await _sequenceSink.dispatchSequence(seq)` (the `_status.state == running` check at line 97 is before the await, and stop() is not serialized by the `_evaluating` lock).

refuted.claim: SEQ-12 (P0), second half: `currentTargetId != null` at entry is a sound test of "this run is mine", so a no-eligible tick can never end an operator's manual sequence.
refuted.how: Same test file, second case, run at HEAD: dispatch target 1, then the autopilot's own run ends by any path other than a natural completion (operator Stop, run failure/abort). Nothing reaches the engine — packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/scheduler_provider.dart:120-131 maps ONLY SequencerEvent_Completed to sequenceCompleted and returns null for Stopped/Failed/Aborted — so `currentTargetId` stays 1 with state=running. The next no-eligible tick took the transient branch and called stopSequence (observed stopCount=1, calls [dispatch-begin, dispatch-end, stop]). At that moment the loaded run is whatever the operator started by hand, and _ExecutorSequenceSink.stopSequence (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/scheduler/scheduler_engine_providers.dart:47) consults no owner — the ActivePlanOwner the dispatch path sets via takeOwnership is never read back. The guard is stale-state, not ownership: it narrows the SEQ-12 P0 rather than closing it.

refuted.claim: s2-native-solver.md (SCI-48): the in-place fallback "reclaims only the files that (a) appeared during this solve, (b) share the frame's base name and (c) are files — pinned by in_place_fallback_reclaims_only_this_solve_s_artifacts and cleanup_keeps_files_that_were_there_before_the_solve, which prove an operator's own sidecar and another frame's files survive."
refuted.how: The sparing rule is a bare STRING-PREFIX match, not a base-name match: /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq2/native/skotiq_native/imaging/src/platesolve.rs:689 `if !name.to_string_lossy().starts_with(stem) { continue; }` — no extension boundary, no separator check. So any file created DURING the solve whose name merely begins with the solved frame's stem is deleted, including a real capture. Refuted with a runnable counter-input: I compiled reclaim_new_artifacts verbatim from HEAD into a standalone binary (/tmp/claude-1000/.../scratchpad/reclaim/main.rs) and ran it on a folder holding M31.fits (the frame being solved, in the pre-solve snapshot) plus, created after the snapshot, M31.ini + M31.wcs (real debris), M31_L_0008.fits (a new light written by the capture pipeline during the solve) and M31_session.log. Output: `M31.ini removed: true / M31.wcs removed: true / M31.fits kept: true / M31_L_0008.fits kept: FALSE / M31_session.log kept: FALSE`. The two repo tests do not catch this because the only 'another frame' fixture they use is M42_L_0001.ini, which shares no prefix with M31_L_0007; and cleanup_keeps_files_that_were_there_before_the_solve exercises the SCRATCH path (temp dir is stageable in CI), so it never reaches reclaim_new_artifacts at all — its keepsake survives because it is in the pre-solve snapshot, not because of the base-name rule. The narrow claim (a) 'pre-existing sidecars survive' HOLDS; the claim that only this solve's artifacts are reclaimed and 'another frame's files survive' does not. Reachability is not hypothetical: the fallback fires when both std::env::temp_dir() staging and the dot-dir-in-parent staging fail, and the second only fails when fs::hard_link is unsupported — i.e. exFAT/FAT32 USB capture drives and SMB shares, which are common capture targets and where ordinary file writes still succeed, so the solver still produces debris and the camera still writes new lights into that folder.
